intent: Draw a line between two rows of an item group.
typical_uses: A divider between two Items inside an ItemGroup

dont_use_when.situation: A divider between sections outside a group of items

invariants.text: ItemSeparator adds a var(--space-2) margin above and below on top of the group's gap.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave a separator exposed to assistive technology inside the group's list
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass aria-hidden="true" on ItemSeparator; the primitive's role separator is not a list item, and the rows' own boundaries already carry the structure

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the separator's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through item.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A decorative divider between two rows

bad.title: A plain Separator between rows
bad.why: Separator is not a member of the group; ItemSeparator is the group's own divider and adds the block margin that spaces it from the rows.
